title: What Blood Does
hook: Blood looks like a single red liquid, but it's really a fleet of specialized parts — each cell type and the fluid itself carrying out a different life-sustaining job.
key_points: Red blood cells carry oxygen from the lungs to every tissue using the protein hemoglobin.
White blood cells defend the body, hunting and destroying invading microbes.
Platelets are cell fragments that clump together to seal wounds and stop bleeding.
Plasma is the liquid that carries cells, nutrients, hormones, and wastes throughout the body.
content_html: Blood may look like a simple red fluid, but it is a busy transport system made of several distinct parts. Roughly half of it is cells; the other half is a watery fluid called plasma. Together they keep every cell in your body fed, oxygenated, defended, and patched up.
extra_html: According to NIH MedlinePlus, blood has four main components, each with a job. Red blood cells, the most numerous, are loaded with hemoglobin, an iron-containing protein that grabs oxygen in the lungs and releases it in the tissues — and gives blood its red color. White blood cells are the immune system's mobile defenders, seeking out and destroying bacteria, viruses, and other intruders. Platelets are tiny cell fragments that swarm to an injury and clump together to form a clot, stopping the bleeding. All of these float in plasma, a mostly-water fluid that also ferries nutrients, hormones, and waste products to where they need to go. Pumped by the heart through the circulatory system, blood touches every corner of the body.

related.title: The Circulatory System
related.hook: Your heart pumps blood through roughly 60,000 miles of vessels, delivering oxygen and fuel to every cell and hauling waste away — about once a minute.

related.title: The Respiratory System
related.hook: With every breath, your lungs trade carbon dioxide for fresh oxygen — the gas swap that keeps every cell in your body running.

flashcards.prompt: What is the main job of red blood cells?
flashcards.back_html: They carry oxygen from the lungs to the rest of the body, using the iron-rich protein hemoglobin that also gives blood its red color.

flashcards.prompt: Which part of the blood is responsible for clotting a wound?
flashcards.explanation_html: Platelets are cell fragments that rush to a cut, stick together, and form a plug that stops the bleeding while the wound heals.

choices.text: The liquid that carries blood cells, nutrients, and wastes

flashcards.explanation_html: Plasma is the pale yellow fluid — mostly water — that the cells float in. It transports nutrients, hormones, and waste products around the body.
